test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb, 2026 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which country has the largest reserve of iron ore in Asia?
solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India** is endowed with the largest reserves of **iron ore** in **Asia**. The country possesses approximately **95%** of the total **haematite** and **magnetite** reserves of the continent.
 
• The iron ore found in **India** is of superior quality, particularly the **haematite** variety, which contains about **60% to 70%** metallic iron. This makes it highly sought after in the international market.
 
• Major iron ore belts in **India** include the **Odisha-Jharkhand belt**, **Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt**, **Ballari-Chitradurga-Chikkamagaluru-Tumakuru belt**, and the **Maharashtra-Goa belt**.
 
• As per the **Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM)**, the state of **Odisha** is the leading producer and also holds a significant portion of the country's **haematite** reserves.
 
• The high-grade **magnetite** ores, which have **magnetic** properties, are found primarily in **Karnataka** (Kudremukh mines), **Andhra Pradesh**, and **Tamil Nadu**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Iron Ore:**

 
 
• **Haematite**: Known as "Red Ore," it has **60-70%** metallic content. It is the most important industrial iron ore in **India**.
 
• **Magnetite**: Known as "Black Ore," it has the highest iron content (up to **72%**) and possesses excellent **magnetic** qualities, useful in the electrical industry.
 
• **Limonite** and **Siderite**: These are inferior quality ores with lower iron content, ranging from **40% to 60%**.
 
 
 
• **Status of Other Countries:**
 
 
• **China**: While **China** is the world's largest producer and consumer of iron ore, its domestic reserves are often of **lower grade** (low iron content), requiring it to import high-grade ore from **Australia** and **Brazil**.
 
• **Russia**: It holds some of the world's largest total reserves, but much of its massive **Kursk Magnetic Anomaly** and Siberian deposits are geographically categorized under **Europe** or **Eurasia** rather than exclusively **Asia**.
 
• **Iran**: It possesses significant iron ore reserves, particularly in the **Yazd** and **Kerman** provinces, but they are smaller in scale compared to **India**.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• In terms of **global production** as of **2023**, **Australia** and **Brazil** lead the world, followed by **China** and **India**.
 
• **India** exports a large quantity of its iron ore to countries like **Japan**, **South Korea**, and **China** through major ports like **Visakhapatnam**, **Paradip**, and **Marmagao**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Industrial Use**: Iron ore is the basic mineral and the backbone of **industrial development**. It is the primary raw material for the **Iron and Steel Industry**.
 
• **Mining Areas**: In **India**, the **Bailadila** mine in **Chhattisgarh** is famous for its high-grade **haematite** which was originally developed for export to **Japan**.
 
• **Geological Surveys**: Regular surveys by the **Geological Survey of India (GSI)** continue to identify new deposits in **Rajasthan** and **Maharashtra**, further solidifying **India's** position in the mineral sector.
